title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages): M is an abelian (profinite) group, M̃ is an extension 1→M→M̃→Γ→1 (eq. 287), and Γ̃ = Im(Γ→Aut M). The objects 𝒳' are equivalent to pairs (E, Θ_M̃), where E is an M-torsor and Θ_M̃ is an action of M̃ on E extending the translation action of M. On the previous page Grothendieck builds a canonical M-equivariant map (290) E → Scind(M̃), the set of sections Γ→M̃. Its image is one M-conjugacy class of sections, and it induces a bijection (291) M^Γ\E ≅ that class. Automorphisms of (E, Θ) are translations by elements of M^Γ.

This page first completes the dictionary. The M̃-action on E defined by Θ_M̃ is the action induced by conjugation on the set of sections, m̃·s = int(m̃)∘s∘int(π(m̃))^{-1}. The relevant M-conjugacy class is therefore necessarily stable under conjugation by arbitrary elements of M̃.

Corollary (292): assume H^0(Γ̃,M) = M^Γ = 0 and H^1(Γ̃,M) = 0. Equivalently, any two splittings of the trivial extension of Γ̃ by M are conjugate by a unique element of M. Then:
- The category of the 𝒳' (equivalently of the pairs (E,Θ)) is rigid: objects have no non-trivial automorphisms, so each object is known up to unique isomorphism once its isomorphism class is known.
- Isomorphism classes, i.e. M̃-stable M-conjugacy classes of sections of M̃→Γ, correspond bijectively (continued on the next page) to quotients M̃̃ of M̃ satisfying three conditions: (a) M injects into M̃̃; (b) Γ' = M̃̃/M acts faithfully on M, so Γ' ≅ Γ̃; (c) the extension M̃̃ of Γ̃ by M is split, i.e. its class in H^2(Γ̃,M) vanishes.

Why the bijection holds. Let N = ker(Γ→Γ̃).
- Class to quotient: for a section s, the subgroup s(N) is unchanged by M-conjugation, since m s(n) m^{-1} = s(n) when n acts trivially on M. M̃-stability of the class makes s(N) normal, and M̃/s(N) is a split extension of Γ̃ by M.
- Quotient to class: the kernel K of M̃→M̃̃ maps isomorphically onto N. Splittings σ of M̃̃→Γ̃ form a single M-torsor because H^0 = H^1 = 0. The preimage of σ(Γ̃) in M̃ is a complement to M, giving a section of M̃→Γ.
- E is recovered as the set of all splittings of M̃̃ over Γ̃, with M̃ acting through M̃̃ by conjugation.

Purpose: this is the general lemma in the post-Longue-Marche notes. It is about to be applied (next page, no. 120) to Γ̃ ≅ Ẑ*×𝔖_3 acting on M^∧. M^∧ is presumably the abelianized profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, or a related module, with Galois acting through the cyclotomic character and 𝔖_3 permuting the punctures. The aim is to show that certain Galois-equivariant torsor/extension data, presumably the next step of the Teichmüller tower / metabelian quotient, are rigid and are determined by a quotient group M̃̃.
errors: No mathematical error. The argument is correct as standard nonabelian-cohomology bookkeeping, provided the M-conjugacy class in question is M̃-stable. Grothendieck notes this stability parenthetically; it is needed for s(N) to be normal in M̃.

Small inaccuracy in phrasing: 'two splittings of a trivial extension conjugate by a unique element of M' is equivalent to H^0 = H^1 = 0 jointly. Uniqueness corresponds to M^Γ = 0 and existence to H^1 = 0. He does add '(i.e. on a M^Γ=0)' for rigidity, so this is only loose wording.
Next page: 'un E-torseur' must be 'un M-torseur'; and 'groupes quotients M̃̃ de M' is corrected to 'de M̃'.

ideas.what: Torsors under M with a compatible M̃-action are equivalent to M̃-stable M-conjugacy classes of sections of M̃→Γ. The M̃-action corresponds to conjugation of sections.
ideas.modern_name: Classification of complements/splittings by nonabelian H^1 (conjugacy classes of sections as an H^1(Γ,M)-torsor)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group cohomology (Schur, Eilenberg–MacLane, Serre's Cohomologie galoisienne)
ideas.where_published: Similar bookkeeping appears in the anabelian letter to Faltings / Esquisse context. The specific form here is in the unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche.

ideas.what: Rigidity criterion: H^0(Γ̃,M) = H^1(Γ̃,M) = 0 implies the category of such objects is rigid (equivalent to a set). Its isomorphism classes biject with quotients M̃̃ of M̃ that are split extensions of Γ̃ = Im(Γ→Aut M) by M.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of torsor/extension data under vanishing of H^0 and H^1; reduction of an extension along the kernel of the action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; in anabelian contexts it is implicit in work on Galois actions on metabelian quotients (Ihara, Anderson, Nakamura)

ideas.what: Intended application: vanishing of H^0 and H^1 of Ẑ*×𝔖_3 with coefficients in M^∧ (abelianized π_1 of P^1−3 points or related), used to rigidify a step of the Teichmüller/Galois tower.
ideas.modern_name: Galois/𝔖_3-cohomology of the abelianized (metabelian) fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Jacobi sums and metabelian quotient, 1985–86); Nakamura; Drinfeld/Ihara for the GT setting
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished Longue Marche continuation notes (the vanishing itself is on the preceding no. 120)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean but standard group-cohomological lemma: classification and rigidity of torsors with compatible extension action via splittings. Its only interest is as part of Grothendieck's unpublished program applying it to Γ̃ ≅ Ẑ*×𝔖_3. That application (the metabelian/abelianized step of the tower) is on neighbouring pages and is broadly paralleled by Ihara's later work. Nothing on this page itself would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'deux scindages d'une cat. triviale de F par M' should read 'deux scindages d'une ext. triviale de Γ̃ par M'.

'est rigide, i.e. un objet est connu : isom. unique près quand on connaît se donne d'isomorphie' should read roughly 'est rigide, i.e. un objet est connu à isom. unique près quand on connaît sa classe d'isomorphie'.
'~ en conjuguant' is likely '= en conjuguant', or a remark that the class is stable under conjugation by arbitrary elements of M̃.
Insertion over 'implique': read 'donc (i.e. on a M^Γ=0)', i.e. the rigidity uses M^Γ = 0.
